:::{#def-local-minimizer}
#### Local minimizer

Let $A \subseteq \reals^p$
and let $f : A \to \reals$ be a [function](sets-functions.qmd#def-function).
A point $x^* \in A$ is a **local minimizer** of $f$
if there is a number $\delta > 0$
such that $f(x^*) \le f(x)$
for all $x \in A$ with
$\norm{x - x^*} < \delta$,
where $\norm{\cdot}$ is the
[Euclidean norm](linear-algebra.qmd#def-euclidean-norm).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-local-minimizer}
#### Local and global minimizers

For $p = 1$, $\norm{x - x^*} = \abs{x - x^*}$.
For example, with $x^* = 1$ and $\delta = 1$,
the condition $\abs{x - 1} < 1$ means $0 < x < 2$.

Every global minimizer (@def-global-minimizer) is a local minimizer:
take any $\delta > 0$.
For example, $x^* = 0$ is a global minimizer of $f(x) = x^2$ on $\reals$,
so it is also a local minimizer.

The converse fails.
In @exr-local-vs-global-min,
$x^* = 1$ is a local minimizer of $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$ (take $\delta = 1$),
but not a global one.

:::
